content.text:
Confirmed: [#13053](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13053) reports a real metadata-extraction bug.

- I reproduced the minimal fixture with Ruby 4.0.5: an empty `postflight_steps` block fails; removing it produces valid JSON.
- The [metadata shim](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/201d/mise/src/system/packages/brew/tap_cask_metadata.rb:166) recognizes ordinary lifecycle hooks but lacks structured `postflight_steps` support.
- Rust already parses structured flight metadata, so adding extraction support fits the existing architecture. Dry-run returns before installation and hook execution.
- There’s a second gap: AeroSpace’s [two commands](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nikitabobko/homebrew-tap/9ac0bfc08904719c52a63101fa7e1e133a23bda2/Casks/aerospace.rb) use `must_succeed: false`, which the current [structured `run` parser](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/201d/mise/src/system/packages/brew/cask/artifacts.rs:708) doesn’t accept.

The fix should serialize these blocks into structured metadata, preserve their path placeholders and failure behavior, and verify extraction never executes commands. Simply ignoring the block would silently omit installation behavior.

No files changed or GitHub replies posted.
make a pr, post a reply
I’ll implement and test the structured metadata support, open a ready-for-review PR, and reply to the discussion with the fix.
